title: I Tried to Fix Blender’s FBX Export and Lost My Mind
description:
The Issue (As I See It):
 - Blender cannot use Autodesk’s FBX SDK due to GPL license incompatibility.
 - Blender’s exporter is a reverse-engineered C implementation.
 - FBX exports are always tagged as Y-Up in metadata—even if you select Z-Up.
 - Blender bakes transforms into bones/meshes instead of relying on clean FBX metadata.
 - Armature space is used directly; this results in a phantom -90° X rotation baked into the root .
originalDescription:
The Issue (As I See It):
 - Blender cannot use Autodesk’s FBX SDK due to GPL license incompatibility.
 - Blender’s exporter is a reverse-engineered C implementation.
 - FBX exports are always tagged as Y-Up in metadata—even if you select Z-Up.
 - Blender bakes transforms into bones/meshes instead of relying on clean FBX metadata.
 - Armature space is used directly; this results in a phantom -90° X rotation baked into the root bone only.
 - Unreal, Unity, and Maya interpret this as an actual transform—leading to inconsistent rigs without user intent.
 - Blender's FBX documentation is too high-level, incomplete, and misleading

Why BetterFBX (and Similar Tools) Work Differently:
 - BetterFBX links to the official Autodesk FBX SDK (closed-source).
 - Can export binary FBX, set true Up/Forward axes, and preserve exact rest/bind poses.
 - Any extension for Blender that uses the FBX SDK is not allowed on Blender’s Extensions platform due to use of binaries and license conflicts.
 - Add-ons using the FBX SDK must bundle a precompiled binary (e.g. .exe or .so). This introduces a security risk—malicious knockoffs of BetterFBX have been reported.

Create Your Own Solution?
 - Like BetterFBX, you can create your own FBX exporter using the FBX SDK
 - It is incredibly tricky to create an exporter that accurately describes data with true axial adaptation.
- FBX SDK documentation is notoriously poorly documented
